summary: Washburn County tower site where a 1934 steel structure replaced a converted 1922 windmill tower; listed as standing, with no source on staffing or access.

facts.design: Steel structure from 1934 that replaced a converted windmill tower built in 1922

events.note: Originally a converted windmill, built by P.A. Mcdonald, according to earlier county forest plans cited in the 2021 plan

evidence.supports: Tower site is the McKenzie Fire Tower site within the McKenzie Unit
evidence.quote: This unit contains the McKenzie Fire Tower site.

evidence.supports: Earlier plans describe a converted windmill built in 1922 by P.A. Mcdonald
evidence.quote: tower was originally a converted windmill, built in 1922 by P.A. Mcdonald, which was
replaced by a steel structure in 1934.

evidence.supports: Plan approved in 2021 by the Washburn County Board
evidence.quote: Approved by Washburn County Board of Supervisors October 19, 2021

evidence.supports: Namekagon River borders the unit on its eastern and northern edges
evidence.quote: The Namekagon River abuts the eastern and northern edge of the unit

evidence.supports: Heavy recreational use from seasonal cabins and homes on surrounding lakes
evidence.quote: This unit receives high levels of recreational use, primarily due to the density of seasonal

evidence.supports: Casey Loop ATV and snowmobile trail runs through and around the unit
evidence.quote: The Casey Loop ATV/Snowmobile Trail runs through, and around the entire unit.

evidence.supports: Snowmobile Trail 8 crosses the far northern edge of the unit
evidence.quote: Snowmobile Trail 8 crosses the far northern edge of the unit.

evidence.supports: Association lists the tower as standing
County list also shows the tower as standing in Washburn County

sources.title: Washburn County Forest Comprehensive Land Use Plan, Chapter 3000.8: McKenzie Unit

notes_for_editor: The 1922 windmill and 1934 steel tower come only from the 2021 county forest plan, which itself relays earlier county plans; no primary record was reached. Status 'standing' rests on the FFLA lists alone. Staffing, current access and visiting rules are not in any source, so they are omitted rather than guessed. The brief's access 'unknown' stands. No corrections to the current record. Possible follow-up: a Washburn County or Wisconsin DNR page on the tower's current condition or public access.
